observation.visible_scene: A pile of split wood — a diagonal plank on the left resting on a front horizontal log, a cylindrical log behind it, and a plank leaning on the right — set against a pure black background, with orange flames burning on the left plank and along the front log and faint smoke rising above.
visible_changes: In the early frames a tall, bright orange flame column rises above the top edge of the left plank, accompanied by a separate flame tongue floating higher in the black space; this column wavers, narrows, and by the middle of the excerpt fades into thin dark wisps with only faint orange tips.

A flame running along the front face of the diagonal plank and down onto the bottom horizontal log persists across the whole excerpt, flickering in shape, with a thin flame line tracking diagonally across the plank surface.
In the later frames new, brighter flame tongues re-emerge from the top corner of the plank, growing and deforming upward, while the high detached flame seen at the start has disappeared.

The wood pieces do not move, fall, or shift position from the first to the last frame; their grain, char marks, and a small knot/hole on the plank face stay in the same place, so the only motion is the flames and smoke.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the fire had just been lit or was already burning before t=0 (it is already active in the first frame).
What occurs after the last frame (whether the flames grow, die out, or the wood collapses).
The cause of the flame flickering and shape changes (airflow/drafts are not visible).
uncertain_details: Whether the high floating flame tongue in the early frames is a distinct flame or illuminated smoke.
The camera appears fixed (wood and background positions constant), but this cannot be confirmed beyond that static evidence.
The exact frame at which the top-edge flames re-brighten is approximate.
